title: Project Appraisal Level 1: Project Finance Foundations
subtitle: How a project loan differs, how to read a feasibility study, and how cost, financing, documents and disbursement fit together
summary: A practical introduction to project lending for Ethiopian credit officers. Follow Sebeta Pasta and Flour PLC from a loan request to a staged disbursement plan, and learn to screen studies, rebuild project cost, test equity and value cash flows.
audience: Credit officers, relationship managers and branch loan staff in Ethiopian banks and microfinance institutions who are new to project and long-term lending.
objectives: Explain how project lending differs from working capital lending and describe the seven stages of the project cycle
Read a feasibility study and flag weak or missing analysis, asking for independent evidence
Build a project cost table, including contingency, interest during construction and initial working capital, and a financing plan that meets the 30% equity rule
Use present value, annuity installments, payback and simple NPV to compare projects and shape a loan
Prepare the document, security, insurance and staged disbursement checklist for a project loan

runningCase.name: Sebeta Pasta and Flour PLC (fictional)
runningCase.text: A new plant near Sebeta will mill wheat and make pasta, with capacity of 30,000 tonnes a year at an average price of Birr 6,000 a tonne. The sponsors, Tolosa Gemechu and Hirut Bekele, already run a flour wholesale business in Addis Ababa and ask for a Birr 70 million long-term loan. Construction takes 12 months; operations start at 60% of capacity, 75% in year 2 and 85% from year 3. Total project cost is Birr 100.1 million, with sponsors' equity of Birr 30.1 million.

modules.title: What Project Lending Is and the Project Cycle
modules.summary: A project loan is repaid by a business that does not exist yet, so the bank judges the plan, the people and the structure instead of a track record.
objectives: Explain why a project loan is repaid from future cash flow rather than an existing trading cycle
Compare project loans and working capital loans on repayment source, evidence, tenor, risks and disbursement
Name and describe the seven stages of the project cycle
Apply a typical Ethiopian bank manual's rules on long-term loans, grace periods and project loan eligibility

lessons.title: A loan to a business that does not exist yet
body: A working capital loan finances a cycle the bank can already see: buy stock, sell it, collect cash, repay. The bank can read past statements and account turnover to judge it.

A project loan finances the creation or expansion of a business: a factory, a hotel wing, a processing plant. On the day of approval there is often no revenue at all. The loan will be repaid from cash the new project generates years from now.

That changes the officer's job. Instead of checking a track record, you test a plan, the people who will carry it out, and a loan structure that protects the bank while the project is still a construction site.
points: Repayment comes from the project's own future cash flow, not the sponsor's existing business
Evidence is a feasibility study, projections and sponsor capacity, not years of history
The bank shares the construction and start-up risk, so structure matters as much as the numbers

example.title: Sebeta Pasta and Flour PLC walks in
example.text: Tolosa Gemechu and Hirut Bekele have sold flour wholesale in Addis Ababa for nine years. Their account shows strong turnover. Now they want Birr 70 million to build a mill and pasta line near Sebeta. Their wholesale history tells the bank they know the market and handle money well, but the loan will be repaid by a plant that has not been built. The officer must appraise the new plant, not the old business.

lessons.tip: Ask early in the first interview: which cash flow will repay this loan, and when does it start?

lessons.title: Working capital loan versus project loan
body: The two products differ on almost every feature. Seeing them side by side helps you place a request in the right product before you start the analysis.

Project loans are longer, rely on forecasts, and carry risks that do not exist in a trading loan: construction delay, cost overrun, untested technology, a new management team and foreign exchange for imported machinery and inputs.

left.title: Working capital loan
items: Repaid from the existing trading cycle
Evidence: past statements, account history
Tenor up to 1 year, often revolving
Main risks: sales, collections, stock
Disbursed to the customer's account

right.title: Project loan
items: Repaid from future cash flow of a new or expanded business
Evidence: feasibility study, projections, sponsor capacity
Tenor 5 to 10 years, with grace
Main risks: construction delay, cost overrun, market, technology, management, foreign exchange
Disbursed in stages against progress, often direct to suppliers and contractors

scenario.title: Birr 8 million for the harvest
scenario.situation: Lemlem Flour Mill PLC asks for Birr 8 million to buy wheat during the harvest season. The mill has operated for six years and will sell the flour within five months. The relationship manager suggests booking it as a long-term project loan to give the customer a lower installment.
scenario.question: What is the right product?
options: A short-term merchandise or working capital loan matched to the harvest and sales cycle
A syndicated loan with another bank
A medium-term equipment loan over four years
A long-term project loan with 24 months of grace
scenario.explain: Buying wheat is a trading cycle that turns into cash within months, so a short-term facility fits. A long tenor would let cash from the flour sales leak away, and there is no capital investment to justify a project loan or a syndicate.

lessons.title: The seven stages of the project cycle
body: Every project, large or small, passes through the same stages. The bank is present in most of them, but its own independent review happens at appraisal.
Knowing the cycle tells you what should already exist when a request arrives, what the bank must do next, and what to watch once money is out.

items.label: Identification
items.text: The sponsor sees an opportunity: a market gap, import substitution, export demand.

items.label: Preparation
items.text: The feasibility study: market, technical, financial, management, legal, environmental.

items.label: Appraisal
items.text: The bank's independent review of every part of the study.

items.label: Approval and negotiation
items.text: Terms, conditions, security and covenants, by the committee with authority.

items.label: Implementation
items.text: Construction and installation; equity in first, staged disbursement, site visits.

items.label: Operation
items.text: Start-up, ramp-up and repayment; follow-up against the plan.

items.label: Evaluation
items.text: Lessons for future lending.

example.title: Sebeta through the cycle
example.text: Identification: wheat flour and pasta demand is rising in Addis Ababa and Oromia, and the sponsors already distribute flour. Preparation: a consultant, Gibe Consulting PLC, wrote the feasibility study. Appraisal: the bank's job, and this course. Implementation: 12 months of construction. Operation: ramp-up from 60% to 85% of capacity. At each stage, ask: what could go wrong here, and who would notice first?

lessons.title: The bank's rules for long-term and project loans
body: Ethiopian banks set their own project lending rules in a credit procedure manual and a separate project financing directive. The figures below are what a typical Ethiopian bank manual sets; your own bank's manual governs your decisions.

Long-term loans run over 5 and up to 10 years for new investments and expansions in sectors such as agriculture, manufacturing, mining, hotels, health and construction. Grace on principal is granted against the projected cash flow and the implementation stage. Because tenors are long, project loans need intensive analysis and close follow-up.
points: Borrower contributes at least 30% of project cost from own funds, committed first and verified at each disbursement
Grace applies to principal; interest accrued during grace is settled as the credit decision sets
A commitment charge applies on undisbursed project loan amounts from the contract signing date
Large projects require an environmental assessment

regulation.source: A commercial bank's Revised Credit Procedure Manual (2025), long-term loans (s.2.1.3) and grace periods (s.2.1)
regulation.text: A typical Ethiopian bank manual defines a long-term loan as maturing over five years and normally not more than ten years, both excluding grace. It may exceed ten years only through rescheduling. Grace of up to 24 months may be granted for long-term loans considering the implementation stage of new or expansion projects, and it covers principal only.

lessons.tip: When you quote a tenor, always say whether grace and the implementation period are inside or outside it.

lessons.title: Is it really a project loan?
body: Not every long-term request is a project. A typical Ethiopian bank manual treats a project loan as finance for capital items, such as buildings and machinery plus start-up working capital, that establishes a business or expands it. Renovation, furniture or machinery that does not raise installed capacity is not a project loan.

The project life must be at least as long as the loan, and the project must generate a financial return. A feasibility study goes to the relevant committee for review before the full loan process starts.

regulation.source: A commercial bank's Revised Credit Procedure Manual (2025), project loan including initial working capital (s.2.2.2)
regulation.text: A typical Ethiopian bank manual sets these project loan features: mainly for capital items and start-up working capital; for expansions, an increase in production capacity of more than 40%; project life at least equal to the loan period; loan tenure not over 10 years excluding grace and implementation periods unless executive management consents. The feasibility study may be waived where the bank has already studied the sector, as with transport trucks and construction machinery. Project loans of any size are approved at head office level, not at district level.

scenario.title: A new wing for Lake Hawassa Resort
scenario.situation: Lake Hawassa Resort PLC, a 60-room hotel, asks for Birr 25 million to build 40 new rooms on adjacent land. Construction will take 14 months. The owner asks for a 10-year loan with grace during construction.
scenario.question: How should the officer classify the request?
options: A renovation loan, since the land is next to the existing hotel
Not a project, because the hotel already exists
An expansion project loan: rooms rise by about 67%, so a long-term loan with grace during construction can be considered
scenario.explain: Forty new rooms on a 60-room hotel raise capacity by about 67%, well above the 40% threshold for an expansion project. A long-term loan with grace matched to construction fits; an overdraft would not match the asset, and this is new capacity, not renovation.

worked.title: Lake Hawassa Resort: does the expansion qualify?

rows.label: Manual threshold for an expansion project
Requested repayment period
rows.value: 10 years after grace, within the manual's cap

worked.note: The request qualifies as an expansion project. Grace should cover construction and the first months of operation, set against the projected cash flow.

lessons.title: Screening a pile of requests
body: Credit officers often receive a mixed set of requests. A quick first screen asks three questions: is this a project, what is the right product, and what tenor makes sense?

Sponsor experience matters as much as the asset. A typical manual expects a pre-established business related to the project, unless the area is innovative or a capable management team can be hired from the market.

items.label: Hotel: 40 new rooms
items.text: Expansion project; long-term up to 10 years with grace during construction.

items.label: Flour mill: wheat stock
items.text: Not a project; merchandise or short-term working capital loan.

items.label: Sesame cleaning plant
items.text: New project; long-term with grace, export proceeds through the bank.

items.label: Five new trucks
items.text: Medium-term vehicle loan with 30% equity; no full project study.

items.label: Clinic MRI machine
items.text: Medium-term equipment loan; a simple viability study of patient volumes.

items.label: Cement plant, no experience
items.text: A project, but the sponsor's inexperience is a fundamental weakness.

scenario.title: Birr 300 million for a cement plant
scenario.situation: Dawit Alemu, a new investor who made his money in real estate and has never run a factory, asks for Birr 300 million toward a cement plant in the Rift Valley. He offers 30% equity and a study prepared by a foreign consultant.
scenario.question: What is the best response?
options: Approve, because 30% equity meets the rule
Treat it as a project but require experienced management, much higher equity and probably a syndicate with other banks
Decline immediately because he has no factory track record
scenario.explain: The request is a genuine project, but lack of sector experience is a fundamental weakness and the size is large for one bank. Experienced management, more equity and a syndicate address those risks; a flat decline ignores the fixes, and 30% equity alone does not cure the management gap.

takeaways: A project loan is repaid from the future cash flow of a new or expanded business, not from the sponsor's existing trade
Project loans are longer, rely on forecasts and carry construction, market, technology, management and foreign exchange risks
The project cycle runs identification, preparation, appraisal, approval and negotiation, implementation, operation and evaluation
A typical Ethiopian bank manual sets long-term loans over 5 and up to 10 years, grace up to 24 months and at least 30% equity from own funds
Expansions qualify as projects only when they raise capacity materially; renovation is not a project

quiz.q: What is the main source of repayment for a project loan?
options: The future cash flow of the project
quiz.explain: A project loan is designed to be repaid from the cash the new or expanded business generates.

quiz.q: At which stage of the project cycle does the bank carry out its own independent review?
quiz.explain: Appraisal is the bank's independent review of every part of the feasibility study.

quiz.q: Why are project loans riskier than short-term loans?
options: Longer tenor, no track record, construction and market risks, and a funding mismatch for the bank
They always carry higher interest rates
quiz.explain: The combination of long tenor, forecasts instead of history and construction risk makes project loans riskier.

quiz.q: What must the borrower do before the bank disburses project money?
options: Hire the bank's engineer as a consultant
Open an account at a second bank
Pay the first installment of principal
Commit and inject its full equity contribution and meet the other conditions precedent
quiz.explain: Equity goes in first, so the owners carry the first risk and the bank does not finance more than its share.

quiz.q: A transport company wants five new trucks. In a typical Ethiopian bank manual, what is the usual treatment?
options: A full project feasibility study and a 10-year loan
A medium-term vehicle loan with about 30% equity, without a full project study
quiz.explain: Manuals waive the full feasibility study for sectors the bank has already studied, such as trucks, and treat it as a medium-term vehicle loan.

quiz.q: Which stage comes immediately after approval and negotiation?
quiz.explain: After the terms are agreed, implementation begins: construction, equity in first and staged disbursement.

modules.title: Reading a Feasibility Study
modules.summary: A feasibility study is the sponsor's sales document, so the officer tests every important assumption against independent evidence.
objectives: Name the parts of a feasibility study and what each should show
Ask the right evidence questions for market, technical, financial, legal and environmental claims
Spot common red flags such as no ramp-up, frozen input prices and unproven price premiums
Use the interview, site visit and credit information checks to verify a study

lessons.title: The study is a sales document
body: Sponsors pay consultants to prepare feasibility studies, and the study is written to win the loan. That does not make it dishonest, but it does make it optimistic.

Your job is not to rewrite the study. It is to find the few assumptions that drive the result, ask what evidence supports each one, and check that evidence yourself. A claim without evidence is treated as unproven until verified.
lessons.tip: For every key claim, ask aloud: what evidence would convince me, and where can I check it independently?

lessons.title: The parts of a feasibility study
body: A complete study covers the people, the market, the plant, the money and the permissions. Missing parts are the first red flag.
Use the cards below as a checklist when a study arrives. If a part is thin or absent, ask for it before you spend time on the financial projections.

items.label: Sponsors and management
items.text: Have they run this kind of business? Who manages day to day?

items.label: Market
items.text: Where do demand numbers come from? Signed buyers? Price against competitors and imports?

items.label: Technical
items.text: Proven technology? Reliable power and water? Raw material all year?

items.label: Organization and staffing
items.text: Are the skills available locally? Who trains the staff?

items.label: Investment cost
items.text: Backed by proformas and engineer estimates? Is there a contingency?

items.label: Financing plan
items.text: Is the equity real and in cash? Is the loan within policy?

items.label: Financial projections
items.text: Reasonable ramp-up, prices and costs? Does cash cover debt service each year?

items.label: Legal
items.text: Investment licence, land lease and permits valid and in the borrower's name?

items.label: Environmental and social
items.text: Waste, emissions, community impact; approved assessment where required?

lessons.title: Testing the Sebeta study claim by claim
body: Read the summary aloud and pause at each claim. Some claims are well supported, some need documents, and one is the weakest point of the project.

For Sebeta, the sponsors' wholesale network is a real strength for the market claim. The raw material claim, local and imported wheat, depends on supply contracts and foreign exchange for imports, and is the weakest point.
points: Market: "demand growing 12% a year; 8% of the Addis market". Ask for the source of the growth figure, competitor capacity and distributor letters of intent
Technical: "Italian milling and pasta line, 30,000 tonnes a year". Ask for the supplier proforma, supplier track record, installation and training terms and warranty
Raw material: "local and imported wheat". Ask for supply contracts and a foreign exchange plan for imported wheat
Utilities: "connected to the grid". Ask for a utility letter and check a backup generator is in the investment cost
Price: "Birr 6,000 a tonne average". Check current wholesale flour and pasta prices and the import parity price
Ramp-up: 60%, 75%, 85%. Reasonable for a plant with an experienced distributor sponsor

worked.title: Sebeta: what a 10% lower price does to year 3 revenue

rows.label: Revenue at Birr 5,400 a tonne (10% lower)

worked.note: A small change in price moves revenue by millions, and most costs do not fall with it. That is why the price claim needs independent evidence, not the consultant's word.

scenario.title: The 12% growth figure
scenario.situation: The Sebeta study says national pasta demand grows 12% a year but gives no source. Hirut Bekele tells the officer the figure is "well known in the industry". The appraisal deadline is in a week.
scenario.question: What should the officer do?
options: Accept it, since the sponsors know the market
Ask for the data source, cross-check with independent sources such as trade associations, competitors and government statistics, and not rely on it until verified
Replace it with 0% growth and reject the project
Ignore market growth because the loan is secured
scenario.explain: Unsourced figures are checked, not accepted or thrown out. Independent verification protects the bank; collateral does not replace a working market.

lessons.title: Red flags in the Bishoftu Poultry study
body: Some studies fail on many points at once. Practicing on a weak study trains your eye for the patterns that recur across Ethiopian project requests.
Each red flag needs evidence or correction before the appraisal can continue. Listing them clearly, with the evidence you need, is a better response than a vague "the study is weak".

example.title: Bishoftu Poultry PLC
example.text: Bishoftu Poultry PLC will produce 2 million broilers a year from day one. The founder, a retired civil servant, will be general manager. Demand is "unlimited" because the population is growing. Feed will be bought locally at current prices for the next 10 years. The selling price is 20% above current market prices because of superior quality. The project cost includes no contingency and no working capital. Land is leased in the name of the founder's brother. An environmental assessment "will be done later". The projected profit margin is 35% from year 1.

left.title: What the study claims
items: 100% capacity from day one
Unlimited demand
Feed at today's price for 10 years
Price 20% above market
No contingency, no working capital
Land leased by the founder's brother
Environmental assessment later
35% margin from year 1

right.title: What the officer asks for
items: A realistic ramp-up and staff readiness plan
Market data, buyers, competitor capacity
Feed price history and a sensitivity test
Evidence of a premium: contracts, tastings, buyers
Rebuilt cost with contingency and working capital
A lease in the company's name
An approved assessment for a waste-heavy activity
Comparison with sector norms

lessons.tip: Feed is the largest and most volatile cost in poultry. A feed price frozen for 10 years is a red flag on its own.

lessons.title: Why new plants ramp up
body: New plants need time to train staff, fix teething problems and win customers. A study that shows full capacity in year one is almost always overstating early cash flow, just when the loan is most exposed.
Sebeta's plan of 60%, 75% and then 85% is more believable because the sponsors already distribute flour and have buyers waiting.

visual.caption: Sebeta revenue: 30,000 tonnes x utilization x Birr 6,000 a tonne (worked example).

worked.title: Sebeta revenue by year

rows.label: If the study had assumed 100% in year 1
rows.value: Birr 180 million, overstating year 1 by Birr 72 million

worked.note: Year 1 is when cash is thinnest and the loan is most exposed. An honest ramp-up protects both the sponsor and the bank.

scenario.title: Full capacity in year one
scenario.situation: Tana Textile PLC's study shows its new weaving plant at 100% capacity in year 1, with all 120 operators hired one month before start-up. The machinery supplier has no installations in Ethiopia.
scenario.question: What should the officer ask for first?
options: Evidence of buyers and staff readiness and why there is no ramp-up, then a revised projection with a realistic ramp-up
A higher interest rate to cover the risk
scenario.explain: The issue is an unrealistic operating assumption. Repricing or shortening the loan does not fix it; a realistic ramp-up in the projections does.

lessons.title: Verifying the study: interview, site and credit checks
body: The bank's normal credit procedure gives you tools to test a study. The interview covers purpose of funds, source of repayment, main customers and suppliers, reliability of raw material supply, alternative markets, management competence, external factors and environmental compliance.

A site visit by at least two bank staff checks that the sponsor's existing business is real, and lets you see the project site, its access road, power and water. A credit information report from the NBE Credit Reference Bureau covers the company, shareholders and guarantors, with their written consent.

regulation.source: A commercial bank's Revised Credit Procedure Manual (2025), environmental analysis (s.4.4.2.2.6)
regulation.text: A typical Ethiopian bank manual requires an environmental assessment of projects proposed for financing. Before deciding on a big project, the bank assesses current legislation that could hurt the project's operation, the project's impact on the natural environment and its waste disposal method, and management's capacity to control the process from raw material input to waste disposal. The legal basis is Ethiopia's Environmental Impact Assessment Proclamation No. 299/2002.

example.title: A visit to the Sebeta site
example.text: Officers Meron Assefa and Kebede Haile visit the Sebeta plot. They find the access road unpaved for the last 2 kilometers and the grid line 800 meters away. The study's cost table has no line for the road or the power connection. They ask Gibe Consulting to add both, with quotations, before the appraisal moves on.

takeaways: Treat a feasibility study as the sponsor's case and test each key assumption against independent evidence
A complete study covers sponsors, market, technical, organization, investment cost, financing, projections, legal and environmental parts
Common red flags: no ramp-up, unsourced demand, frozen input prices, unproven premiums, missing contingency, land in the wrong name
Large projects need an environmental assessment before the bank decides
The interview, site visit and NBE Credit Reference Bureau report are your tools to verify the study

quiz.q: What evidence supports a machinery cost in a feasibility study?
options: A supplier proforma invoice plus quotations or an engineer's estimate for installation
quiz.explain: Machinery cost should rest on a supplier proforma and documented installation estimates.

quiz.q: Why is "100% capacity from year one" unrealistic for a new plant?
options: Demand always falls in year one
Machines run slower in year one by law
New plants need time to train staff, fix teething problems and win customers
quiz.explain: Ramp-up reflects real start-up problems, so year one output is usually well below capacity.

quiz.q: Which document proves the right to use the project site?
options: The land lease certificate or title in the borrower's name
quiz.explain: The lease certificate or title must be in the borrower's own name.

quiz.q: A study's market section quotes no source. What do you do?
options: Ask for the source, check independent sources and not rely on the figures until verified
Accept it if the sponsor is experienced
quiz.explain: Unsourced numbers are verified before they are used.

quiz.q: In the Sebeta study, which claim did the trainer identify as the weakest point?
options: Raw material supply, local and imported wheat
quiz.explain: Wheat supply depends on contracts and foreign exchange for imports, so it is the weakest point.

quiz.q: Which of these is a red flag for land in a project study?
options: Land leased in the name of the founder's brother
A lease longer than the loan tenor
Land leased in the company's name
quiz.explain: Land must be in the borrower's name to support the project and to be mortgaged to the bank.

modules.title: Project Cost and the Financing Plan
modules.summary: Rebuild a project's cost from its parts so nothing is missing and nothing is inflated, and check that the owners really carry at least 30% of it.
objectives: List the eight project cost components and the evidence for each
Calculate contingency and interest during construction
Build a financing plan and test it against the 30% equity rule
Judge whether cash and in-kind contributions count as equity

lessons.title: The eight components of project cost
body: A project's cost is everything that must be paid before the project can stand on its own cash flow. Leaving out a component does not make it disappear; it makes the project run out of money halfway through.
Each component needs its own evidence. If the sponsor cannot document a line, the officer either rebuilds it or asks for proof.

items.label: Land
items.text: Lease prepayment, site preparation. Evidence: lease contract, receipts.

items.label: Building and civil works
items.text: Factory, warehouse, offices, fence, roads. Evidence: bill of quantities, engineer's estimate.

items.label: Machinery
items.text: CIF price, duties and clearing, inland transport, installation. Evidence: proforma, freight and duty estimate.

items.label: Vehicles
items.text: Trucks, forklifts. Evidence: proforma invoices.

items.label: Pre-operating costs
items.text: Study, licences, staff training, trial runs. Evidence: budget, quotations.

items.label: Contingency
items.text: Typically 5% to 10% of building and machinery for price and quantity changes.

items.label: Interest during construction
items.text: Interest that accrues before the project earns income.

items.label: Initial working capital
items.text: First raw materials, stock, receivables, cash.

lessons.tip: Machinery cost is never just the CIF price. Add duties, clearing, inland transport and installation.

example.title: The missing transport line at Jimma Coffee Processing
example.text: Jimma Coffee Processing PLC lists its pulping and drying machinery at the CIF price of Birr 18 million. Officer Yonas Tadesse asks for the freight forwarder's estimate and the installer's quotation, and finds that duties, clearing, inland transport from Djibouti and installation add Birr 3.2 million. Without that correction the project would have stopped with the machines sitting in a warehouse.

lessons.title: Contingency and interest during construction
body: Contingency covers price increases and quantity changes during construction so the project does not stall for lack of funds. It is usually 5% to 10% of building and machinery, based on the analyst's judgment of how firm the quotations are.

Interest during construction (IDC) is the interest that accrues on the loan before the project earns income. If the loan is drawn evenly, on average about half of it is outstanding during construction, which gives a simple estimate.

visual.caption: A quick estimate for a loan drawn evenly over the construction period.

worked.title: IDC for a Birr 40 million loan drawn over 18 months
worked.note: IDC is a real cost of the project. It belongs in the cost table and is financed like any other item.

lessons.title: Sebeta's cost and financing plan
body: Here is Sebeta's cost rebuilt from its parts. Note that machinery includes duties, clearing and installation, and that contingency is 5% of building and machinery.
The financing plan just meets the 30% rule: Birr 26.1 million cash plus the land lease already paid of Birr 4.0 million gives equity of Birr 30.1 million, or 30.1% of cost.

worked.title: Sebeta Pasta and Flour PLC: project cost (Birr millions)

rows.label: Machinery: CIF 33.0 + duties and clearing 3.0 + installation 4.0

worked.note: Two traps: leave out IDC or contingency and the project runs short mid-construction; count equity before it is verified and the bank ends up financing more than 70%.

visual.caption: Sebeta's Birr 100.1 million project cost by component.

lessons.title: The equity rule and what counts as equity
body: A typical Ethiopian bank manual requires the borrower to contribute at least 30% of project cost from own funds, never from borrowing, committed before the bank disburses. Equity puts the owners' own money at risk first and gives the bank a cushion.

Equity can be cash or in-kind assets valued by the bank, such as land already paid for or civil works already done. Verify cash equity through bank statements and block it; have the bank's engineer value in-kind contributions. The asset must belong to the company and be suitable for the project.

visual.caption: Equal to total project cost less the minimum 30% equity.

regulation.source: A commercial bank's Revised Credit Procedure Manual (2025), collateral rules for vehicles and machinery (s.6.1.2 and s.6.1.3)
regulation.text: A typical Ethiopian bank manual does not accept vehicles or construction machinery more than 10 years from the date of manufacture as collateral; those aged 10 to 15 years are accepted only exceptionally with senior approval. Used vehicles are valued at the lowest of the insurer's value, an external assessor's value or the head office market value. Apply the same caution when an old asset is offered as equity.

scenario.title: Equity from another bank
scenario.situation: The sponsors of Gondar Dairy PLC need Birr 18 million of equity for a Birr 60 million project. They plan to take a Birr 18 million personal loan from another bank, secured on their houses, and inject it as cash equity.
scenario.question: How should the officer treat this equity?
options: Accept it, because cash is cash
Accept it if the other bank's loan is longer than this one
Reject it as equity: borrowed money adds hidden debt and puts none of the owners' own funds at risk
scenario.explain: The rule requires own funds, not borrowing. Borrowed equity means the owners risk nothing of their own and the project carries debt the bank did not appraise.

lessons.title: Other sources: supplier credit, external loans and syndicates
body: Besides equity and the bank loan, projects may use supplier credit (the machinery supplier lets the buyer pay over time), loans from foreign lenders, or other banks in a syndicate when the project is too large for one bank.
Foreign currency borrowing brings its own rules and risks. Repayment must be serviced in foreign currency, so the officer checks how the project will earn or buy it.

regulation.source: NBE Directive No. FXD/01/2024, Foreign Exchange Directive (as amended)
regulation.text: The NBE's market-based foreign exchange directive covers external loans, including a 60:40 debt-to-equity cap for foreign investors, along with export repatriation, retention accounts and dividend repatriation. Bank manuals add that supplier credit needs NBE approval under these rules.

example.title: Sebeta's machinery offer
example.text: The Italian supplier offers to finance part of the Birr 33 million CIF price over three years. The officer notes that this would add a foreign currency liability that the plant, selling only in Birr, cannot easily service. The bank recommends keeping the machinery inside the Birr loan, paid through an import L/C, and flags foreign exchange availability as a risk in the appraisal.

lessons.title: Case study: Adama Cement Block Factory
body: The sponsor presents (Birr millions): land lease 1.0 already paid; building 6.0; block machine CIF 7.0, duties and clearing 1.0, installation 0.5; a used truck 2.5 that the sponsor already owns, offered as equity; pre-operating 0.6; working capital 1.5. There is no contingency and no IDC. Equity offered is land 1.0, truck 2.5 and cash 1.5, a total of 5.0. The loan requested is 15.825 at 15%, with 9 months of construction.
Rebuild the cost with a 5% contingency and IDC, then test the equity.

worked.title: Adama Cement Block Factory rebuilt (Birr millions)

rows.label: Gap
rows.value: about 1.5 more cash, or the loan drops to about 15.2

worked.note: The used truck counts only after the bank's engineer values it; over 10 years old it is unacceptable as collateral and doubtful as equity. The land counts only if the lease is in the company's name.

scenario.title: The sponsor pushes back
scenario.situation: Adama's sponsor, Abdi Mohammed, says contingency and IDC are "bank inventions" and asks the officer to approve Birr 15.825 million on the original Birr 20.1 million cost. He says he will "find money" if costs rise.
scenario.question: What is the best response?
options: Remove the working capital line to make the numbers fit
Approve as requested to keep the client
Include contingency and IDC, and require about Birr 1.5 million more cash equity or reduce the loan to about Birr 15.2 million
Double the contingency to 10% and approve the full loan
scenario.explain: Contingency and IDC are real costs. Once included, equity is only 23%, so either the sponsor adds cash or the loan is cut to keep the bank at 70%. Removing working capital would just move the shortage to start-up.

takeaways: Project cost has eight components: land, building, machinery, vehicles, pre-operating costs, contingency, IDC and initial working capital
Machinery cost includes CIF price, duties, clearing, inland transport and installation
IDC can be estimated as loan x rate x drawdown years x average share drawn
A typical Ethiopian bank manual requires at least 30% equity from own funds, committed and verified before disbursement
In-kind equity counts only when owned by the company, suitable for the project and valued by the bank's engineer

quiz.q: Why include a contingency in project cost?
options: It is optional and usually left out
To cover price increases and quantity changes during construction so the project does not stall
quiz.explain: Contingency protects the project from running short of money during construction.

quiz.q: Loan Birr 40 million at 15%, drawn evenly over 18 months. Estimate IDC.
quiz.explain: 40 x 15% x 1.5 x 50% = Birr 4.5 million.

quiz.q: Project cost is Birr 50 million. What are the minimum equity and maximum loan?
quiz.explain: 30% of 50 is 15, leaving a maximum loan of Birr 35 million.

quiz.q: Can equity come from a loan from another bank?
options: Yes, if it is in cash
Yes, if the other bank agrees
No; borrowed equity adds hidden debt and puts none of the owners' own money at risk
Only for projects under Birr 10 million
quiz.explain: Equity must come from own funds, never from borrowing.

quiz.q: In Sebeta's plan, what makes up the sponsors' equity of Birr 30.1 million?
options: Cash of 26.1 plus the land lease already paid of 4.0
quiz.explain: Sebeta's equity is Birr 26.1 million cash plus Birr 4.0 million of land lease already paid.

quiz.q: Which is NOT part of the machinery cost line?
quiz.explain: Raw material stock belongs in initial working capital, not machinery.

modules.title: Time Value of Money for Project Decisions
modules.summary: A Birr received in year 8 is worth much less than a Birr today, and that one idea drives loan installments, payback and NPV.
objectives: Calculate future value and present value
Use the annuity factor to compute equal loan installments
Compute payback and simple NPV and explain what each tells the bank
Choose between projects and explain how cash flow timing shapes the loan structure

lessons.title: Future value and present value
body: Money today can be invested to earn a return, so a Birr today is worth more than a Birr later. Future value grows today's money forward at a rate; present value brings future money back to today.
For project lending, present value matters most: the loan is paid out now, and the project's cash comes back over many years.

visual.caption: And the reverse: FV = PV x (1 + r) to the power n.

worked.title: Warm-up: Birr 100,000 today or Birr 150,000 in 3 years?
worked.note: At 15%, Birr 150,000 in three years is worth slightly less than Birr 100,000 today.

lessons.tip: In a spreadsheet, =PV(rate, n, 0, -FV) gives the present value of a single future amount.

lessons.title: Annuities and loan installments
body: An annuity is a series of equal payments. Its present value is the payment times the annuity factor. Turn that around and you get the equal installment that repays a loan.
The annuity factor at 15% for 5 years is 3.352. You will use this number many times in this course.

parts.label: Annuity factor: (1 - (1 + r) to the power -n) / r

worked.title: Equal annual installment on a Birr 1,000,000 loan
worked.note: The same factor scales: a Birr 2 million loan on the same terms needs about Birr 596,631 a year.

example.title: Hana Girma's bakery oven
example.text: Hana Girma of Dire Dawa borrows Birr 2 million at 15% over five years to install a new oven line. Using the annuity factor of 3.352, the officer shows her the equal installment of about Birr 596,631 a year, then checks that the bakery's projected cash after costs, about Birr 800,000 a year, covers it with room to spare.

lessons.title: Choosing the discount rate
body: For the bank, the discount rate is the required return on the project: at least the lending rate, often higher to reflect project risk. The rate must cover the project's risk and the bank's costs and return, not only its funding cost.

Under the NBE's current interest rate directive, each bank sets its own lending rates, so there is no single national rate to plug in. Use your bank's approved rate for the borrower's risk grade and add a margin for project risk where your policy says so.

regulation.source: NBE Directive No. NBE/INT/13/2026, Interest Rates (As Amended) Directive
regulation.text: Effective January 9, 2026, each bank freely sets its deposit and lending rates. Rates must be approved in writing by the bank's board on explicit written criteria and reported to the NBE, along with monthly weighted average rates. It repeals and replaces all earlier NBE interest rate directives.

scenario.title: Which rate for Sebeta?
scenario.situation: The bank's cost of funds is about 11% and Sebeta's loan is priced at 16%. Gibe Consulting's study discounts Sebeta's cash flows at 10% and reports a large positive NPV.
scenario.question: What should the officer do?
options: Ignore NPV and look only at collateral
Re-run the NPV at a rate at least equal to the 16% lending rate, and higher if project risk warrants
Accept 10%, because it is the consultant's professional choice
scenario.explain: A rate below the lending rate flatters the project. The required return must at least cover what the bank charges, and project risk can justify more.

lessons.title: Payback and NPV
body: Payback is the number of years until cumulative cash flow covers the investment. It is simple and useful for liquidity, but it ignores cash after payback and the timing of money.

NPV is the sum of all cash flows, each discounted to today, minus the investment. A positive NPV means the project earns more than the discount rate; a negative NPV means it destroys value at that rate.

left.title: Payback
items: Years to recover the investment
Easy to explain to sponsors
Good signal of liquidity and early risk
Ignores cash after payback
Ignores the time value of money

right.title: NPV
items: Value created after discounting
Uses every year's cash flow
Depends on the discount rate chosen
Positive means the project beats the rate
Spreadsheet: =NPV(rate, year1:yearN) + year0

worked.title: A Birr 500,000 machine saving Birr 150,000 a year for 5 years
worked.note: The same project passes or fails depending on the rate demanded.

example.title: Mekele Packaging's new cutter
example.text: Mekele Packaging PLC wants to buy a Birr 500,000 cutting machine that its owner, Selam Tesfaye, says saves Birr 150,000 a year for five years. At the bank's 15% the NPV is barely positive; at 18% it is negative. The officer advises Selam to get a firmer quote on savings before borrowing, since a small shortfall would wipe out the gain.

lessons.title: Case study: Project X or Project Y?
body: Both projects cost Birr 100 million. Project X's cash flows (Birr millions) are 60, 40, 20, 10 and 0 in years 1 to 5. Project Y's are 10, 20, 50, 70 and 70.
Payback favors X; NPV favors Y. Y creates far more value but its early cash flows are thin, so it needs a loan with grace in years 1 and 2. X could repay a short loan fast but barely earns its cost.

worked.title: Payback and NPV at 15% (Birr millions)

rows.label: Project Y payback: 80 recovered by year 3, 20 of 70 in year 4

worked.note: Choose Y for value, and shape the loan to its cash flow with grace in the early years.

visual.caption: Worked example: Y creates about 24 times more value than X at 15%.

scenario.title: The sponsor prefers fast payback
scenario.situation: Tigist Worku must choose between Project X and Project Y for her agro-processing group. Her board likes X because it pays back in 2 years. The bank's required return is 15%.
scenario.question: What should the officer advise?
options: Choose X, because payback is the safest measure
Choose neither, since both cost Birr 100 million
Choose Y for its much higher NPV, with a loan that has grace in years 1 and 2 to match its thin early cash flow
Choose X and lend over 10 years
scenario.explain: Y creates far more value at the required rate. Its slow start is a structuring issue, solved with grace, not a reason to pick a project that barely earns its cost.

takeaways: PV = FV / (1 + r) to the power n; a Birr later is worth less than a Birr today
Installment = Loan / annuity factor; the factor at 15% for 5 years is 3.352
Discount at the required return on the project: at least the lending rate, often higher for project risk
Payback measures liquidity but ignores cash after payback and the timing of money
A positive NPV means the project earns more than the required rate; cash flow timing shapes tenor and grace

quiz.q: PV of Birr 1 million received in 2 years at 16%?
Annual installment on Birr 2 million over 5 years at 15%?
What does a negative NPV mean?
options: The project makes an accounting loss
The project earns less than the required rate and destroys value at that rate
quiz.explain: NPV compares the project's return with the discount rate; negative means it falls short.

quiz.q: Name one weakness of payback.
options: It ignores cash after payback and the time value of money
quiz.explain: Payback stops counting at the recovery point and treats all years' money equally.

quiz.q: Why does the bank discount at a rate higher than its cost of funds?
options: The rate must cover the project's risk and the bank's costs and return, not only its funding cost
Because the NBE sets a fixed discount rate
quiz.explain: A required return includes risk and margin on top of funding cost.

quiz.q: Which project needs grace in its early years: X (60, 40, 20, 10, 0) or Y (10, 20, 50, 70, 70)?
quiz.explain: Y's thin early cash flows cannot carry full debt service in years 1 and 2.

modules.title: Project Documents, Security and Staged Disbursement
modules.summary: Protect the bank while a project is still a construction site: the right documents, a security package that grows with the project, and money released only against progress.
objectives: Prepare the full document checklist for a project loan
Design a security and insurance package that grows from construction to operation
List the conditions precedent before first disbursement
Plan and control a staged disbursement schedule with site visits

lessons.title: Documents for a project loan
body: A project loan file is larger than a trading loan file because the bank must confirm the company, the site, the plant, the money and the permissions before any money moves.
Collect the documents early and check each is valid, in the borrower's own name, and consistent with the feasibility study.
points: Application and feasibility study
Investment licence and commercial registration
Memorandum and articles of association with authority to borrow and mortgage
Land lease certificate in the company's name
Approved building permit and drawings, and the bill of quantities
Machinery proformas and supplier contracts; the construction contract
Environmental assessment where required
Evidence of equity
Tax clearance and TIN
Credit reports on the company, shareholders and guarantors

example.title: The Sebeta file is almost complete
example.text: Sebeta's officer Meron Assefa ticks off the checklist and finds two gaps: the articles of association do not yet give the general manager authority to mortgage company assets, and the building permit covers the mill but not the pasta warehouse. She asks the sponsors to pass a shareholder resolution and to extend the permit before the file goes to the committee.

lessons.title: Security that grows with the project
body: At the start of construction, the bank's security is thin: a land lease right and some foundations. It grows as buildings rise and machinery arrives. The security package must follow that growth.

Typical security: a mortgage over the land lease right and buildings, the project's machinery once delivered, a business mortgage over the plant registered with the competent registry, assignment of insurance, and personal or corporate guarantees from sponsors where needed.

regulation.source: A commercial bank's Revised Credit Procedure Manual (2025), collateral (Chapter 6); Movable Property Security Right Proclamation No. 1147/2019
regulation.text: A typical Ethiopian bank manual accepts a building under construction as collateral when at least 60% of the work is complete for residential and 65% for commercial or factory buildings, with lower completion possible for project finance. A business mortgage covers plant, machinery and equipment, verified by year of make and serial numbers, and security interests are also registered on Ethiopia's movable collateral registry under Proclamation No. 1147/2019.

worked.title: Sebeta: security coverage at completion (Birr millions)
worked.note: Coverage is lower during construction, so sponsor guarantees are useful until completion, when the main risks of delay and overrun sit with the sponsors.

lessons.title: Insurance from construction to operation
body: Insurance must follow the same path as the security. During construction, a contractor's all risks or "in course of construction" policy covers the works. Imported machinery needs marine and transit cover until it reaches the site.

Once operating, the plant needs fire and allied perils and machinery breakdown cover. Every policy is endorsed to the bank as first beneficiary, and the officer tracks renewal dates, because an unpaid premium means no cover.

items.label: Construction
items.text: Contractor's all risks (in course of construction) policy on the works.

items.label: Machinery in transit
items.text: Marine and transit insurance on imported machinery to the site.

items.label: Start-up and operation
items.text: Fire and allied perils, and machinery breakdown, bank as first beneficiary.

items.label: Every year
items.text: Renewal checked, premiums paid, values updated.

regulation.source: A commercial bank's Revised Credit Procedure Manual (2025), insurance (Chapter 7); Insurance Business Proclamation No. 746/2012, art. 48
regulation.text: A typical Ethiopian bank manual requires all mortgaged or pledged property to carry appropriate insurance endorsed to the bank. For construction in progress, the application states the current value, the value when completed and the construction material. Plant and machinery under a business mortgage are insured at the collateral value. The Insurance Business Proclamation sets the principle of no premium, no cover.

lessons.title: Conditions precedent before first disbursement
body: Conditions precedent are the things that must be true before the bank releases the first Birr. They make sure the legal protection, the owners' money and the permits are in place before the bank takes construction risk.
A commitment charge applies on undisbursed project loan amounts from the contract signing date, so sponsors have a reason to meet the conditions quickly.

items.label: Contracts signed and registered
items.text: Loan and mortgage contracts signed, collateral registered.

items.label: Equity injected and verified
items.text: Cash equity spent or blocked, in-kind assets valued.

items.label: Interest during grace arranged
items.text: Pre-deposited in a blocked account or arranged as agreed.

items.label: Insurance endorsed to the bank
items.text: Construction cover in place, bank named.

items.label: All permits in place
items.text: Licences, building permit and environmental approval.

scenario.title: Can we release tranche 1 now?
scenario.situation: Sebeta's contractor, Meki Valley Builders PLC, is ready to start the superstructure and asks for tranche 1. The loan contract is signed, but the mortgage is not yet registered and Birr 6 million of the sponsors' Birr 26.1 million cash equity is still unspent.
scenario.question: What should the officer do?
options: Release tranche 1 to avoid delaying construction
Hold the release until the mortgage is registered and the full cash equity is spent and verified
Release tranche 1 and ask the sponsors to sign a personal guarantee
scenario.explain: Registration and full equity are conditions precedent. Releasing early would make the bank finance more than its share without registered security; a guarantee does not replace either condition.

lessons.title: Staged disbursement against progress
body: Release funds against certified progress, such as engineer's certificates or supplier documents, in proportion to equity already spent. Pay contractors and suppliers directly or through import L/Cs, not into the borrower's general account.
Visit the site before each tranche. A typical Ethiopian bank manual follows up project loans at each disbursement phase and then yearly. If warning signs appear, stop and refer back to the committee.

worked.title: Sebeta's disbursement schedule (Birr millions)

rows.label: Tranche 0: sponsors' cash equity of 26.1 fully spent on land, foundations and machinery deposit; contracts registered
Tranche 1: building 50% complete, engineer's certificate; paid to contractor
Tranche 2: machinery L/C opened for the balance of CIF; paid to supplier via L/C
Tranche 3: building complete, machinery arrived and cleared; paid to contractor, customs, transporter
Tranche 4: installation, trial run, initial working capital; paid to installer and raw material suppliers

worked.note: Each trigger is a fact the officer can verify on site or on paper before the money moves.

items.label: Tranche 0
items.text: Equity 26.1 spent, contracts registered. Bank: 0.

items.label: Tranche 1
items.text: Building 50% complete. Bank: 15.0 to contractor.

items.label: Tranche 2
items.text: Machinery L/C opened. Bank: 25.0 via L/C.

items.label: Tranche 3
items.text: Building complete, machines cleared. Bank: 15.0.

items.label: Tranche 4
items.text: Installation, trial run, working capital. Bank: 15.0.

scenario.title: Tranche 3, but the machines are at the port
scenario.situation: Meki Valley Builders asks for Sebeta's tranche 3 of Birr 15 million. The engineer certifies the building complete, but the milling machines are still at the dry port awaiting clearance.
scenario.question: What should the officer do?
options: Release the full Birr 15 million, since the building is done
Refuse any release until the plant is running
Release the money to the sponsors to pay customs themselves
Release only the part tied to completed building work, and visit before releasing more
scenario.explain: Disbursement follows verified progress. The building part is earned; the machinery part is not until the machines are cleared and on site, and paying the sponsor directly risks diversion.

lessons.title: Capstone: Sebeta's checklist
body: Bring the course together by preparing Sebeta's full package: the document checklist, the security package at completion, the conditions precedent, an insurance plan for construction and operation, and two things to check on every site visit.

The point is not paperwork for its own sake. Each item closes a specific risk you identified in earlier modules: the weak wheat supply, the cost overrun risk, the equity trap and the construction delay.

items.label: Documents
items.text: Licence, registration, articles, lease, permits, contracts, equity proof, TIN, credit reports.

items.label: Security
items.text: Mortgage on land lease and building; business mortgage or pledge on machinery and vehicles, registered.

items.label: Conditions precedent
items.text: Contracts registered, equity verified, interest arrangement, insurance, permits.

items.label: Insurance
items.text: Contractor's all risks, marine and transit, then fire, allied perils and machinery breakdown.

items.label: Site visits
items.text: Progress against schedule and funds released; machinery quality and quantity; equity spent as claimed.

example.title: What the Sebeta visit found
example.text: Before tranche 2, officers Kebede Haile and Meron Assefa compare the engineer's certificate with what they see. The building is 55% complete, matching the funds released. They also check the sponsors' receipts for the machinery deposit against the supplier's acknowledgment. Both match, and they recommend opening the L/C.

lessons.tip: On every site visit, compare three things: physical progress, money released and equity spent. Any gap between them is a warning sign.

takeaways: A project loan file covers the company, the site, the plant, the money and the permissions, all in the borrower's name
Security grows with the project, so sponsor guarantees help until completion
Insurance moves from contractor's all risks to fire, allied perils and machinery breakdown, always endorsed to the bank
Conditions precedent: contracts signed and registered, equity verified, grace interest arranged, insurance endorsed, permits in place
Disburse in tranches against certified progress, pay suppliers directly, and visit the site before each release

quiz.q: Why are project loans disbursed in tranches?
options: To reduce interest during construction to zero
To match money to verified progress, ensure equity goes first and prevent diversion
Because the NBE forbids single disbursements
quiz.explain: Staged release keeps the bank's money tied to real, verified progress.

quiz.q: Which insurance covers a building under construction?
options: Contractor's all risks (in course of construction)
quiz.explain: Contractor's all risks covers works in progress.

quiz.q: Why might the bank ask sponsors to guarantee the loan until completion?
options: Because security is incomplete during construction and the main risks of delay and overrun sit with the sponsors
Because the law requires it for all loans
quiz.explain: Until the plant is complete, collateral is thin and sponsors control the main risks.

quiz.q: Which is a condition precedent before first disbursement?
quiz.explain: Equity must be in and verified before the bank releases funds.

quiz.q: How should a machinery tranche normally be paid?
options: In cash to the general manager
To the supplier through an import L/C
quiz.explain: Paying suppliers directly or through L/Cs prevents diversion of funds.

quiz.q: When does a commitment charge apply on a project loan in a typical Ethiopian bank manual?
options: Only if the loan becomes overdue
On undisbursed amounts from the contract signing date
On the whole loan from the first disbursement
quiz.explain: The commitment charge applies to the undisbursed balance from contract signing.

exam.q: Rift Valley Juice PLC wants to replace its old bottling machine with a new one of the same capacity. Under a typical Ethiopian bank manual, how is this classified?
options: A project loan, because machinery is a capital item
Not a project loan, because it does not raise installed capacity; a term or equipment loan fits
exam.explain: Manuals treat machinery that does not increase installed capacity as outside the project loan definition.

exam.q: A biscuit factory plans to raise output from 10,000 to 12,500 tonnes a year. Does this meet a typical manual's expansion project test?
options: Only if a feasibility study is waived
Yes, if the loan is over Birr 10 million
No, a 25% increase is below the more-than-40% threshold
exam.explain: 2,500 / 10,000 = 25%, below the more-than-40% capacity increase that defines an expansion project.

exam.q: Which stage of the project cycle comes directly before appraisal?
exam.explain: Preparation produces the feasibility study that the bank then appraises.

exam.q: Under a typical Ethiopian bank manual, what is the normal maximum tenor of a project loan?
options: 10 years excluding grace and implementation periods, unless executive management consents
exam.explain: Project loan tenure is capped at 10 years excluding grace and implementation, and must not exceed project life.

exam.q: Sebeta's study reports a 10% price drop would "not matter". At 85% of 30,000 tonnes, how much year 3 revenue would a fall from Birr 6,000 to Birr 5,400 a tonne remove?
exam.explain: 25,500 tonnes x Birr 600 = Birr 15.3 million a year.

exam.q: A tannery study says its environmental assessment "will be done later". What should the officer do?
options: Require an approved assessment before the appraisal is completed and make it a condition precedent
Proceed, since the assessment is the sponsor's business
exam.explain: Waste-heavy projects carry legal and reputational risk; the manual requires environmental assessment before a big project decision.

exam.q: Which feasibility study claim most needs independent evidence?
options: A selling price 20% above market because of superior quality
exam.explain: A price premium drives revenue and is easy to overstate, so it needs buyer contracts or market evidence.

exam.q: Loan Birr 50 million at 15%, drawn evenly over 18 months. Estimate IDC.
exam.explain: 50 x 15% x 1.5 x 50% = Birr 5.625 million, about 5.6.

exam.q: Loan Birr 30 million at 16%, drawn evenly over 12 months. Estimate IDC.
exam.explain: 30 x 16% x 1 x 50% = Birr 2.4 million.

exam.q: A project has building of Birr 20 million and machinery of Birr 30 million. What is a 5% contingency?
exam.explain: 5% x (20 + 30) = Birr 2.5 million.

exam.q: Project cost is Birr 120 million. The sponsors offer cash of Birr 25 million and land lease already paid of Birr 8 million, in the company's name. What must happen?
options: The land is excluded and the loan is approved at Birr 95 million
Sponsors add about Birr 3 million cash, or the cost is cut, because equity is 27.5% against 36 required
exam.explain: Equity 33 / 120 = 27.5%; 30% needs Birr 36 million, so Birr 3 million more is required and the loan stays at no more than Birr 84 million.

exam.q: A sponsor offers a 12-year-old truck as in-kind equity. How should it be treated?
options: Treat it with great doubt: vehicles over 10 years are not accepted as collateral in a typical manual, and any value needs the bank's engineer
Accept it if it is painted in company colors
Accept it at the sponsor's purchase price
exam.explain: Old vehicles carry little reliable value; the manual rejects vehicles over 10 years as collateral, so their value as equity is doubtful.

exam.q: PV of Birr 500,000 received in 3 years at 15%?
Equal annual installment on Birr 10 million over 5 years at 15%?
A machine costs Birr 800,000 and saves Birr 250,000 a year for 5 years. The annuity factor at 18% is 3.127. What is the NPV at 18%, and the decision?
exam.explain: 250,000 x 3.127 = about 781,800, less 800,000 = about -Birr 18,200; it fails at 18%, though it would pass at 15%.

exam.q: A project costs Birr 60 million and earns 15, 20, 25 and 30 million in years 1 to 4. What is its payback?
exam.explain: Cumulative cash is 15, 35 and then 60 at the end of year 3.

exam.q: Project A has NPV +3 and payback 4 years; Project B has NPV -1 and payback 2 years. Which creates value?
exam.explain: Only a positive NPV creates value at the required rate; fast payback does not save B.

exam.q: The engineer certifies the building complete but the machines are still at the port. The contractor requests the full tranche. What do you do?
options: Release the tranche to the sponsors to pay customs
Release only the part tied to completed building work and visit before releasing more
exam.explain: Only verified progress earns money; the machinery part waits until the machines are cleared and on site.

exam.q: At completion, Sebeta's security is land and building about 34, machinery 40 and vehicles 4 (Birr millions) against a Birr 70 million loan. What is the coverage, and what does it imply during construction?
options: About 111%; coverage is lower during construction, so sponsor guarantees are useful until completion
About 111%; no further security is ever needed
About 90%; the loan should be cut
exam.explain: 78 / 70 is about 111% at completion, but during construction the assets are not all in place, so guarantees bridge the gap.

exam.q: Which set lists the right conditions precedent before first disbursement?
options: Year 1 sales report, dividend policy, staff contracts
Contracts signed and registered, equity verified, grace interest arranged, insurance endorsed, permits in place
Plant at 60% capacity, first installment paid
exam.explain: These five conditions secure the bank's legal position and the owners' money before construction risk is taken.

sources: Erudite Africa training module: Project Appraisal Level 1: Project Finance Foundations (October 2026)
A commercial bank's Revised Credit Procedure Manual (August 2025), unnamed
NBE directives as listed in the lessons: FXD/01/2024 and NBE/INT/13/2026
Ethiopian laws as cited: Environmental Impact Assessment Proclamation No. 299/2002, Movable Property Security Right Proclamation No. 1147/2019, Insurance Business Proclamation No. 746/2012
